name: Cloudflare Secrets Store

status.note: In open beta since 9 April 2025, with one store and up to 100 secrets per account.

summary: Account-level secrets that are written once, can never be read back, and are bound by reference into any Worker or AI Gateway that needs them.
intro: Ordinary Workers secrets belong to one Worker: set with `wrangler secret put`, they show up on that Worker’s `env`, so a key used by ten Workers is stored ten times and anyone who can edit a Worker can change its secrets. Secrets Store holds secrets for the whole account instead. You create a secret (any string up to 65,536 bytes) in the dashboard, the API or with `wrangler secrets-store secret create`, and give it scopes that say which products may use it: `workers`, `ai-gateway` or both. After that its value can’t be decrypted or read through the API or dashboard by anyone; only the bound service gets it at runtime.

A Worker gets a `secrets_store_secrets` binding with a store ID and secret name, and reads the value with an async `await env.MY_KEY.get()`. AI Gateway can reference a stored provider key instead of receiving it in every request header. Two checks guard each use: the person or API token binding the secret needs the Super Administrator or Secrets Store Deployer role (or an Edit token), and the secret’s scopes must include the consuming product. Values are encrypted with per-secret data keys wrapped by a key-encryption key, and copied to every Cloudflare server. Locally, `wrangler dev` uses secrets created without `--remote`; production values never reach your laptop.
strengths: One source of truth: rotate a key once and every Worker bound to it sees the new value
Separates duties: admins create secrets, deployers can only bind them, reporters see only metadata, and changes go to the audit log
Write-only by design: after creation nobody, including Cloudflare staff, can read the value back through the API or dashboard
Scopes stop a secret meant for AI Gateway from being bound into a Worker, and the reverse
limits: Still in open beta: one store per account and at most 100 production secrets
Only two consumers so far, Workers and AI Gateway; other Cloudflare products still keep their own secrets
Reading a value is an async call per binding, unlike per-Worker secrets that sit directly on `env`
CI tokens that deploy Workers with these bindings need Secrets Store Edit permission, not Read, and the service is unavailable in the Cloudflare China Network

snippet.title: Create an account secret, bind it to a Worker, read it in code
source: npx wrangler secrets-store store list            # find the store ID
--name OPENAI_API_KEY --scopes workers --remote   # prompts for the value

story: Environment variables and secrets arrived in Workers in 2020, and by 2025 there were millions of them, many duplicated: the same API token copied into ten scripts had to be created and rotated ten times, and anyone with access to a script could edit its secrets. Other Cloudflare products, from Access service tokens to AI Gateway provider keys, kept secrets of their own.

On April 9, 2025, during Developer Week, Mia Malden, Mitali Rawat and James Vaughan launched Cloudflare Secrets Store in beta, starting with Workers. Secrets were encrypted with a two-level key hierarchy, guarded by role-based access control, and pushed to every server with Quicksilver, so a Worker finds its secrets wherever it runs. Every account could create up to twenty secrets for free while pricing was being finalized.

In May 2025 the limit rose to 100 secrets per account, and in August 2025 AI Gateway started using Secrets Store for bring-your-own provider keys, with a scope of its own. Cloudflare has said it plans per-store bindings, multiple stores per account and customer-specific data keys.

choices.why: Once created, a value is not readable by developers, admins or Cloudflare employees; only the permitted service uses it at runtime, so a leaked dashboard session does not leak keys.

choices.choice: Separate roles for managing and deploying
choices.why: Per-Worker secrets follow Workers permissions, so whoever can edit the Worker can edit the secret. Account-level roles let security teams own the values while developers only bind them.

choices.choice: Envelope encryption with frequently refreshed data keys
choices.why: Each secret is encrypted with a data key, and the data keys with a key-encryption key whose root never leaves a secure system, which keeps the impact of a single exposed key small.

timeline.text: Workers gains per-script environment variables and secrets
